custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Create a Part Library entry with no part behind it for this test, entry A: create a part at the test location, then delete it, so the entry stays with "Total parts" 0.
  • Use a desktop browser that can open a second tab on the same ShopView address, signed in as the same user.
  • Start in browser tab 1 on the Part Library page (Parts in the top bar, then Part Library in the left menu).

How to set this up on the QA site (https://sv10647.qa.shopview.com):

  • Admin at the test location: on the QA site's sign-in screen choose Admin. The test location is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919; its name shows in the box at the top right. If another name shows, click that box, click the name beside Change Location: and pick Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • To create a part: click Parts in the top bar, Inventory in the left menu, then New Inventory Part. Fill Description and Part Number (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-C425620-A for part A, -B for part B), pick a Category, type a Cost and a Sell Price, type the Quantity in the bin row (the location's bin, for example General Storage, is offered), then click Save. Leave Track quantities and cost of goods on for a tracked part; click it off for an untracked part. Add Bin Location adds a second bin; Vendor, Manufacturer, Core Charge, Min, Max and Tags are in the same window. Parts that must start with the same text all start ZZAUTOTEST-PL-C425620-, so searching for that finds them all.
  • The Search box above the Inventory list opens when you click Search (the magnifier).
  • Second tab: open a new browser tab on the same QA site address (https://sv10647.qa.shopview.com); you stay signed in as the same user.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Entry A is listed.

Step 2:

  • Its detail page opens and shows "Total parts" 0.

Step 3:

  • The "Edit Library Part" window opens and its Delete button, bottom left, is enabled, because no part uses the entry yet.

Step 4:

  • A second tab opens.

Step 5:

  • Tab 2 shows the Parts left menu.

Step 6:

  • Tab 2 shows the Inventory page.

Step 7:

  • The "New Inventory Part" window opens in tab 2.

Step 8:

  • Description shows entry A's description.

Step 9:

  • Part Number shows entry A's number.

Step 10:

  • Category shows the category you picked.

Step 11:

  • Cost shows 10.00.

Step 12:

  • The window closes in tab 2 and the part is saved.

Step 13:

  • Tab 1 still shows the Edit Library Part window: it was not reloaded.
  • Its Delete button is still enabled: it shows the entry as it was when the page opened, before tab 2 saved a part on it.

Step 14:

  • The confirmation asks "Are you sure you want to delete this library part?"

Step 15:

  • The delete is refused: a red message reads "This Part Library entry is in use and cannot be deleted.", with a smaller second line "Please try to resolve this."

Step 16:

  • The red message has closed on its own after about 3 seconds.

Step 17:

  • Tab 1 shows the Parts left menu.

Step 18:

  • The Part Library page opens.

Step 19:

  • Entry A is still listed.

Step 20:

  • Its detail page shows "Total parts" 1: the part saved in tab 2 uses it.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, version 35 (edited 27 Oct 2026 by Chris Ward), read 28 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10647, story SV-10825 (Story 12, Call the Shared Parts List the Part Library), story SV-10826 (Story 13, The Part Dialog), story SV-10824 (Story 11, The Part Library Is Browse and Edit Only)

  • S12-R11: “Refusals that name the shared list read: "This Part Library entry is in use and cannot be deleted.", "Part Library entry not found.", "Part Library entry not found", "Part Library entry not found for ID: {id}.", "Part Library entry not found for part number: {part number}.", "Part Library entry missing category." and "A part from the Part Library must have Vendor as its source."”
  • S12-R11a: “Of the S12-R11 refusals, normal screen use reaches "This Part Library entry is in use and cannot be deleted.", "Part Library entry not found." (S11-E4) and "Part Library entry not found for ID: {id}." (opening the address of a deleted entry). "Part Library entry not found" and "Part Library entry missing category." appear only with damaged or legacy data, and the "for part number" and "must have Vendor as its source" refusals are not raised today. All are renamed so no old wording remains; the unreachable ones are verified in code review, not on screen.”
  • S12-R13: “Deleting a Part Library entry asks "Are you sure you want to delete this library part?"”
  • User Feedback Summary: “Part Library entry in use deleted | "This Part Library entry is in use and cannot be deleted." | Error toast, fades after 3 seconds”
  • Story 13, context note: “Context note: every refusal sent by the system, the rows that fade after 3 seconds, also shows a second, smaller line under the message: "Please try to resolve this." Messages the screen builds itself carry their own second line, as listed, or none.”
  • S11-R3c: “While an inventory part, an open part request or a part return still uses the entry, the Delete button is disabled and hovering it shows "Part cannot be deleted. Please delete related parts first."”
  • S11-E5: “The Delete button in the "Edit Library Part" window reflects the entry as it was when its detail page opened. If the last part, part request or part return using the entry goes away elsewhere, Delete becomes enabled after the page is reloaded.”

From: Product's answers to questions 13 to 27 (Chris Ward, 27 Oct 2026, Google Doc https://docs.google.com/document/d/1pkAPGqWVTdtYorNN4SVNl9HkHxuuB9czro_y2DbUeEM/edit, saved word for word in full-pass-2026-10-27/ANSWERS-13-27-2026-10-27.md), read 28 Oct 2026

  • Chris Ward, 27 Oct 2026, answer 15: “No. Delete stays disabled until the page is reloaded (S11-E5). Note that an open part request or a part return using the entry also keeps Delete disabled, not only an inventory part (S11-R3c).”
  • Chris Ward, 27 Oct 2026, answer 24: “Only these show through normal screen use: "This Part Library entry is in use and cannot be deleted.", "Part Library entry not found." (save an entry deleted in another tab, S11-E4), and "Part Library entry not found for ID: {id}." (open the address of a deleted entry).”

From: Tech plan "Parts Lifecycle Update — Technical Implementation Plan" (7 Oct 2026, written against PRD v22; re-shared by the QA lead on 27 Oct 2026, unchanged), read 27 Oct 2026

  • §1 Clarifications, Q9 S12-R11 copy: “Delete refusal "This Part Library entry is in use and cannot be deleted."”

References from Design

Design canvas "Parts Lifecycle Update" (https://claude.ai/artifact/Vz6rprcWyP16tYxzM1kdeE), 13 Oct 2026 copy, unchanged when re-read on 27 Oct 2026: board "7.2 An entry opens its detail page". Compare the screen with the pictures below; the expected results above come from the quotes above.

The board 7.2 note quoted below says the entry "can be edited and deleted" on its page. Product confirmed on 27 Oct 2026 (answer 20) that this note is out of date: the detail page has no Delete, and Delete is in the "Edit Library Part" window. The expected results follow the PRD.
